title: Halo's Next Chapter: A Famous Game Hero Changes Hands Again
summary:
One of the most famous video game heroes ever is at a crossroads. Halo, the science-fiction shooter series starring the armoured super-soldier Master Chief, is changing hands again, and fans are wondering whether its best days are behind it.

Halo began in 2001, created by a studio called Bungie. After Bungie left, a new team — 343 Industries, now renamed Halo Studios — took over. According to the writer, Halo 4 and Halo 5 did not really move the series forward, and Halo Infinite, which tried to recapture the feel of 'old Halo' inside an open world, did better but still fell short of the glory days.

This year brought Halo: Campaign Evolved, a full remake of the original game's story mode and Xbox's second attempt at refreshing the 2001 classic. The writer calls it perfectly fine — a shiny 2026 version of the game that made audiences fall in love with the series — but hardly the rescue Halo needs.

Now Xbox has shaken things up again. Activision, the company behind Call of Duty, is taking over development, leaving the Halo Studios veterans as a smaller support team, in a change that also means more layoffs. Rumours suggest a reboot, possibly retelling Master Chief's origins. The writer argues that later games turned Chief from a skilled soldier into a larger-than-life figure, shrinking the wider world around him.

Still, there are reasons for hope. In May 2026, insider Rebs Gaming reported that remakes of Halo 2 and Halo 3 were in development, and Xbox has already found success with remastered games such as The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered. For now, though, Master Chief's future is cloudier than ever.
why_it_matters: Halo is one of the most famous game series in the world, so who develops it shapes what millions of players will play next. The change also affects the jobs of the people who have built the series for years.

background_read: Halo is a long-running series of science-fiction shooter games starring Master Chief, an armoured super-soldier, and it is one of Xbox's most famous series.
Big game series are made by development studios, and when a series changes studio, the new team brings its own ideas and style, which is why fans watch handovers like this so closely.
Game companies often remake or remaster classic games for modern machines, because famous old games can win new players and please long-time fans.
Halo has already passed from one studio to another before, and each change has shaped what the next games feel like.
